premise.claim: The port allocator can randomly assign the same port to different pods. When a pod uses hostNetwork: true, those ports occupy the node's network namespace, so two pods with the same allocated port must not be scheduled on the same node. (PR body, Motivation)
premise.reportedComponent: pkg/port-allocator (random allocation + pod injection); kube-scheduler NodePorts plugin as the spreading mechanism
premise.patchedComponent: pkg/port-allocator (manager.go injection, parser.go protocol validation, type.go)
premise.evidence: RandomAllocator guarantees uniqueness only within one AllocateBatch call (random.go doc comment); per-pod PodScoped allocations are separate calls. Deterministic repro with a 1-port range: two AllocateBatch calls both return 30000; on base d162208e the injected host-network pods declare zero container ports, so the scheduler's NodePorts plugin sees nothing (results/unit-base-p0.txt). On head c05052c2 both pods declare hostPort == containerPort == 30000 (results/unit-head-full.txt).

integration.cmd: KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=$(if [ -x bin/setup-envtest ]; then bin/setup-envtest use 1.31.0 --bin-dir bin -p path; elif command -v setup-envtest >/dev/null 2>&1; then setup-envtest use 1.31.0 -p path; else go run sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/tools/setup-envtest@release-0.20 use 1.31.0 -p path; fi) go test -count=1 ./test/envtest/testcase/verifypr532/ -json

liveNote: AC5 (two host-network pods sharing a RoleScoped port land on different nodes) is covered by the PR's own e2e test 'should spread host-network pods sharing a role-scoped host port', which requires >=2 Ready+schedulable nodes and therefore skips on the single-node CI kind cluster; not run in this harness (live layer out of scope). The scheduler-side mechanism is upstream kube-scheduler NodePorts behavior. Note: kube-apiserver defaultHostNetworkPorts defaults hostPort=containerPort for hostNetwork pods at admission, so persisted-pod assertions cannot distinguish controller-set from apiserver-defaulted hostPort.
